correctness.rationale: Lucas digitwise binomial congruences prove parity rigidity exactly for primes 3 and 5. The first five central binomial factorizations prove the five-branch sharp obstruction for every p>=11, with p=7 checked directly. Reciprocity+CRT count 12 classes per joint four-symbol pattern modulo 840; Dirichlet gives exact densities. For p=5, Lucas digit restriction and the generating polynomial (2+z)^L prove all three exact residue counts and imaginary-part imbalance. Tests on 668 primes, 1400 exceptional-prime indices, 16 CRT patterns, and 6 complete digit levels corroborate these proof steps.

originality.rationale: The 2013 motivating residue conjecture and 2014 modulus-five allowed-residue counterexample are correctly attributed to their authors and are not claimed as original. The separately proved sharp first-discrepancy classification, prime densities and exact level-by-level coefficient counts are not implied by any of the inspected published statements. Originality remains qualified by missing complete 2014 full text and unindexed-literature possibility.

value.rationale: The precise questions are motivated by the documented modulus-five failure of a general residue-distribution conjecture. A complete rigidity classification for all odd primes, a sharp universal first defect, positive-density arithmetic partition and a quantitative block-frequency law explain the exceptional phenomenon structurally, rather than being an unmotivated finite slice. The exact frequency asymmetry is meaningful independently of an unproved downstream application.
